title: Agent mail send (opt-in per chat) + plugins/mail
what:
Perch side:
- <home>/mail-agents.json {id: {on, at}} (statefile pattern, 0600). Off by default. A fork has a new id, so it starts off.
- POST /hub/sessions/<id>/mailsend {on}, operator only.
- POST /hub/mail/a/send {node, mesh?, subject, text}, through AG's mail scope:
  - 403 'agent mail is off for this chat' unless the chat has opted in
  - node verified or self; text ≤ 64 KiB; at most 10 per hour per chat (429)
  - the same argv as an operator send, but with --from=minerva-agent, so Aoide's letter and the receiver's card both say an agent sent it (ruling 4: origin in the record). The chat id stays local.
  - sent.jsonl line with origin agent:<chat> and from 'minerva-agent'
plugins/mail (MIT): plugin.rn, tools/send.rn (tool mail_send, mutating, un-vouched so it asks in manual and auto), README, LICENSE. The service descriptor uses the mail token file and the url file.
Page: webui/term/notes/agentmail.js registers a loaded section, 'agent mail: off [ turn on ]' / 'on since 14:02 [ turn off ]', plus the last agent sends.
tests:
tests/mail_agent.rs with FAKE_AGENT_CALL:
- off gives 403; turning on then gives 202 with an origin line
- the argv has --from=minerva-agent
- the 11th send within an hour gives 429
- a test-process curl gets 403
- a fork id is off
plugins/mail/tests/shape.sh against a stub server on 127.0.0.1:48119.
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48120: toggle the opt-in in the loaded tab, run a fake-door send, and see the sent row.
risk: The opt-in is per chat id and lives on disk. A chat rooted at $HOME could write mail-agents.json directly (the same exposure chat-modes.json already has). The XS review states it. --from is attribution, not proof.
